asks: What load is one device sized for?
answer: Silo is sized for two loads. The common one is main with a few agents and one or two computers beside it, on a Mac with 16 GB of memory. The heavy one is about 16 agents working at once in main, on a Mac with 32 GB. With a macOS main, at most one of the computers beside it is macOS, since Apple allows two macOS computers running on a Mac. For an agent that checks its work in an iOS simulator, the load is the number of simulators booted, about 3.4 GB each, so many agents share a few, with a maximum booted at once that Silo shows. Whether each load fits is measured with the benchmark of `memory-handling-measured`, and what does not fit lowers the maximum Silo shows (`running-computers-maximum`).
